facts: The probe intended to increment the ボーカル allocation counter by one.
After the click, the counter changed from 0/20 to 1/20 and a vocal skill-entry panel opened.
The original probe expected only the counter change and therefore initially recorded the panel opening as an anomaly.
Later calibration observed the same allocation-plus-panel behavior for two stat columns.
The calibration resolution states that allocation inherently opens the corresponding skill-entry panel and that the click did not miss.
The allocation remained uncommitted and 決定 was not pressed.
inferences: The counter increment establishes that the intended control effect occurred, while repeated calibration explains the panel as an inherent side effect.
An unexpected additional effect is not sufficient for a mis-click verdict when the probe criterion failed to enumerate allowed and forbidden side effects.

Before any mis-click verdict, the test must define complete expected and disallowed outcomes, freshly verify the pre-click state and target, observe the full post-click state, and repeat a controlled calibration that isolates competing causes.
The stale-coordinate hypothesis is not supported for this incident after the repeated calibration result.
unknowns: The panel's precise gameplay semantic identity remains unknown in the calibration record.
The mechanism by which the open panel gates 決定 remains unknown.
The behavior is established only for the recorded calibration scope and is not proven universal across layouts or viewports.
reason: The intended counter effect occurred and the additional panel was reproduced as intrinsic control behavior; complete probe criteria and controlled calibration must precede a failure classification.
